overview: A single 'Urls' feature on the platform kit. Writes (create link) go through IUrlService → IUrlRepository (EF Core, unique index on Code). The redirect hot path resolves codes through ICacheService (cache-aside, 10 min TTL) and enqueues a ClickEvent on IBackgroundQueue<ClickEvent>, so analytics never add latency; ClickRecorder writes clicks in batches and increments a denormalised ClickCount. Stats are aggregated from click events per link.

fields.notes: unique index; generated base62 (7 chars) or custom alias

nfrPatterns.nfr: Read-heavy redirects (~100 reads per write), p95 latency

nfrPatterns.pattern: Stateless instances; random IDs + unique constraint + retry on collision
nfrPatterns.buildingBlock: Base62CodeGenerator + unique index + UrlService retry loop

nfrPatterns.pattern: Rate limiting per client + validate at the edge

nfrPatterns.buildingBlock: ClickEvent stores referrer host + UA family only

decisions.title: 302 instead of 301 redirects
decisions.rationale: 301 is cached by browsers, so repeat clicks would never reach the service and analytics would undercount.
decisions.alternatives: 301 (cacheable, less load but breaks analytics); 307 (equivalent for GET).

decisions.title: Random base62 codes instead of a sequential counter
decisions.decision: 7-character codes from a CSPRNG; unique index + up to 5 retries on collision.
decisions.rationale: No coordination between instances (scale-out), codes are not enumerable; 62^7 ≈ 3.5e12 keeps collisions negligible.
decisions.alternatives: DB sequence + base62 (needs a single sequence, enumerable); hash of URL (same URL → same code, collision handling still needed).

decisions.title: Asynchronous, batched click recording
decisions.decision: Redirects enqueue click events; a background worker writes them in batches of up to 200 or every 500 ms.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the hot path to a cache lookup; one transaction per batch instead of one per click relieves the single SQLite writer.
decisions.alternatives: Synchronous insert per redirect (simple, but couples redirect latency to DB writes); external broker (durable, needed on Kubernetes, overkill locally).

decisions.title: Denormalised click counter
decisions.decision: Maintain ShortUrl.ClickCount alongside raw click events.
decisions.rationale: Total clicks are read often; avoids COUNT(*) over a growing table.
decisions.alternatives: Always aggregate from events (simpler, slower as data grows).

risks: Clicks in the in-process queue are lost if the process crashes before a flush (accepted locally; use a durable broker on Kubernetes).
Per-instance memory cache can serve a deleted/changed link until TTL expiry when several instances run (no delete/edit in this version; Redis removes the issue).
Anonymous creation can be abused for spam/phishing links; mitigated only by rate limiting in this version.
